script: "I cooked my dad a gourmet lunch, but my 13yo half brother ATE IT ALL, leaving me with nothing.". So my mom goes homeless, and my dad lets her and her kids crash at our place out of the goodness of his heart. I mean, I guess that's cool, right? My dad's always been super particular about his food, hates sandwiches and leftovers, so I started cooking him lunch to take to work. It's a nice gesture, if I do say so myself. I get home from school, and I am starving, and I see that my portion of food is gone. I am like, what the heck? My half-brother is just chillin' on the couch, and I am about to ask him what's good, and he tells me he ate my food. He says he was really hungry, and it smelled too good to pass up. I am like, really? You know I was counting on that food. He says he's sick of sandwiches, and I always make these nice meals that he can't have 'cause I don't share with him. I lose my cool, and I tell him it's not okay to just eat my food. I mean, he's been making sandwiches all day, like it's no big deal. I send him to his room, and my mom comes home, and she's all upset. She's like, "Girl, you're being a selfish bitch for not sharing with your brother." I am like, what? That's not my job. I cook for my dad, not for anyone else. She's all like, "I'll pay you for the meal," like that's even the point. And then she tells me it wouldn't kill me to cook for them too. Honestly, I am done. I am done with her attitude and expecting me to take care of everyone else. I told her this is her job, not mine, and that I had to go hungry for an hour because of her son. She calls me an asshole, but like, what even is that? I am just trying to take care of myself here. My dad comes home, and I fill him in on what happened. He's like, "Hey, sorry about that, kiddo." And I am like, "Thanks, dad." It's all good. In the end, my dad actually understood where I was coming from. He even agreed that I shouldn't have to cook for my half-brother. He said, "You're right, kiddo. You cook for me, not for them." It felt good to know my dad had my back.
